html:
The first written collection of Jewish oral law, compiled around 200 CE in Galilee by Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi, "Judah the Prince", head of the Jewish community under Rome. Until then the teachings of the rabbis had been passed on by memory.

After the Romans destroyed the Second Temple in 70 and crushed the Bar Kokhba revolt in 135, the old centres of Jewish life were gone. Writing the law down kept it from being lost. The Mishnah is written in Hebrew and arranged in six orders: farming, festivals, marriage, civil and criminal law, the Temple, and ritual purity. It often records the disagreements of named sages rather than a single ruling.

Later rabbis in Galilee and in Babylonia studied and debated it, and their discussions, the Gemara, were added around it. Together they form the Talmud: the Jerusalem Talmud of about 400 and the larger Babylonian Talmud of about 500. The Mishnah is the base of rabbinic Judaism, the form of Judaism that has lasted to the present.
sum: The first written collection of Jewish oral law, compiled around 200 CE in Galilee by Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi, "Judah the Prince", head of the Jewish community under Rome. Until then the teachings of the rabbis had been passed on by memory.
